hero.eyebrow: FRC Team 6962 · Khan Lab School · Mountain View, CA
hero.title: Students build the robot.
hero.lede: Antares is a FIRST Robotics Competition team of 6th through 12th graders. Every January we get 8 weeks to design, build, wire and program a 120-pound robot, then take it to the field.

communities.title: Three communities, one team
communities.lede: If you are meeting Antares for the first time, these are the pieces worth knowing.

sponsors.title: Companies and foundations that make the season possible

photo.body: Sponsor logos travel with us. They are on the shirts in the stands, on the pit display, and on the robot itself at every event we attend.

match.title: 3 vs 3
match.lede: Each team brings one student-built robot. Every match pairs three red-alliance teams against three blue-alliance teams, and lasts approximately two-and-a-half minutes.

studentLed.title: Seven years to become the person who teaches it
studentLed.lede: FRC typically serves 9th through 12th grade. Antares starts in 6th grade, so students have enough seasons to learn a discipline, lead it, and hand it on before they graduate. Mentors provide safety, technical context and coaching. Students make the decisions.

cta.title: Back a team that hands the tools to students
cta.body: Sponsorship funds robot parts, registration, travel and the shop where 6th graders learn to build. Partnership tiers start at $1,000, and in-kind support and employer matching are welcome.

hero.title: Students make the decisions
hero.lede: Mentors bring safety, technical context and coaching. Students do the rest: they make the engineering calls, run the budget, find the sponsors, and teach the group coming up behind them.

ladder.title: Knowledge that carries forward
ladder.lede: FRC typically serves 9th through 12th grade. Because Antares starts in 6th grade, a student can spend seven years on the team: long enough to learn a discipline properly, lead it, and train a replacement before they leave.

subteams.title: Eight disciplines, all student run
subteams.lede: Every one of these has a student lead, a training curriculum and a job to do before the robot ships.

school.title: Khan Lab School
school.lede: Antares is based at Khan Lab School, a nonprofit school built to explore what mastery-based, student-directed learning looks like in practice. The team extends that model into a leadership development and engineering program with real deadlines, public performance and student ownership.

frc.title: What FIRST Robotics Competition is
frc.lede: Every January, FIRST reveals a brand-new game. Teams get 8 weeks to build a robot for it, then compete at district events and regionals. Matches last two and a half minutes and pair alliances of three teams against three.

awards.title: A growing record
awards.lede: Antares awards span technical performance, imagery, team culture and individual student leadership.

cta.title: Support students from 6th grade through 12th
cta.body: Sponsorship and donations pay for the parts, the registration fees and the shop time that make this program possible.

blogs.title: Written by students, every week
blogs.lede: Each entry covers what the team designed, what broke, and what changed as a result.

cta.title: Come and watch a competition
cta.body: Bay Area events are free to attend and run all weekend. Email the team and we will tell you where we will be and where to find our pit.

hero.title: Every season since 2018
hero.lede: One new robot a year, built in eight weeks by students. These are the machines, the awards, and the lessons that shaped the program.

cta.title: Help fund the next robot
cta.body: Every season on this page was paid for by sponsors, families and in-kind support. The next one needs the same.

hero.title: How we teach a 6th grader to build a robot
hero.lede: Antares publishes its training curriculum so other teams can use it. These materials were written for our own students, so some of it is specific to how we work.

cta.title: Use anything here
cta.body: These materials are published for the FRC community. If something is unclear or you want the editable version, email the team and we will send it over.

hero.title: Partner with the students building what's next
hero.lede: Antares gives companies a credible way to support student-led engineering while building visibility with STEM-focused students, their families, mentors, and the wider Silicon Valley and California robotics communities.

value.title: Repeated visibility with future technical talent
value.lede: The season runs from the January kickoff through April, with events most weekends. Sponsor branding travels the whole way: on the robot, the pit display, the shirts and the build blog.
value.note: Recognition varies by tier and by event policy. A recent example: sponsor-supplied cutting mats and gloves went into gift bags for other teams at regional competitions.

first.title: FIRST builds technical talent at scale
first.lede: Antares turns a national program into a local team your employees can meet, follow and support during the season.

levels.title: Pick a tier, or design one with us
levels.lede: Each tier adds to the one before it. Multi-year, in-kind, matching and employee-expertise partnerships are all welcome.
levels.note: Final benefits follow sponsor, school, team and event requirements.

cta.title: A student will answer your email
cta.body: Tell us what your company cares about and we will come back with a proposal that fits. In-kind tools, machining and mentorship count too.

hero.title: Where the money goes
hero.lede: Antares publishes its budget split so sponsors can see exactly what their contribution funds. These are the planned shares of the 2025-26 expense budget.

chart.title: Fifty-five percent of it is the robot
chart.lede: Robot parts, stock materials and equipment together account for 55% of planned spending. The rest keeps students registered, fed, traveling, practicing and reaching the community.
chart.note: Rounded percentages, totaling 100%. A gift noted “Antares, Team 6962” is a restricted gift: Khan Lab School has to spend it on the Antares program.

offsite.title: A hands-on employee robot experience
offsite.lede: An Antares Mission partner could host a supervised team offsite built around the Antares robot: a student briefing on how it works and what failed, a safety orientation and supervised driving practice, then short driving and scoring challenges for employees.
offsite.note: This is a proposed concept. Final scope depends on venue, robot availability, a partner team for any second robot, adult supervision and school safety approval.

cta.title: Fund a season
cta.body: Partnership tiers start at $1,000, and in-kind tools, machining, fabrication and expertise are just as useful as cash.

hero.title: Every gift buys parts, hours and a place at the event

family.title: Family giving is the base the season stands on
family.body: Corporate sponsorship is what makes an ambitious season possible, but family contributions are what make it dependable. They arrive early, they are not tied to a company's budget cycle, and they cover the unglamorous things: the replacement gearbox in week five, the meal on a competition Saturday, the registration deposit that has to be paid before anyone has seen the game.
family.note: Gifts of any size help, and many employers will match them, which quietly doubles what a family can do. If your workplace has a matching program or a donor-advised fund, ask us and we will send you exactly what their portal needs.

checklist.title: Two things that keep the gift on track

cta.title: Not sure which route fits?
cta.body: Email the team and we will help you work out the simplest way to give, including whether your employer will match it.

methodOnline.title: Online
methodOnline.note: Card or ACH through the school

methodMatching.title: Employer matching and donor-advised funds
methodMatching.note: Double a gift through your workplace
